identity.realm: Ceiling stated as the twenty-ninth gate, and the mechanism is accumulation rather than a wall. Every gate an unwritten body passes writes a fresh requirement into that body, and the frame cannot satisfy the requirement because its own life law has no slot to hold one, so the contradiction finally exceeds what the frame will bear at the twenty-ninth and the thirtieth resolves all of it at once. She is at the eleventh and has stopped there on purpose. The thirtieth is not described anywhere in this record and she is not the person who will describe it: her whole method is that a body carrying a requirement it cannot meet is a legible document, and a body that resolves everything at once is not.

appearance.presentation: A tall, narrow, forty-one-year-old woman who stands with her weight even on both feet and her hands loose at her sides, in the deliberate plainness of somebody who has decided to be read. She wears the collar high and the sleeves long because the requirements she carries are legible along the frame and she has stopped trying to arrange them.
appearance.age: Forty-one on a span that runs longer than a commonborn's by an order of magnitude. The record does not put a figure on it and neither does she; what it says is that each requirement she passes adds one the frame cannot hold, which is a cost measured in specifications rather than in years.
appearance.build: An unwritten frame is a body that has been written past its own law and kept, and hers has been written eleven times. She is not heavier than she was at thirty and she is considerably harder to describe: the frame has acquired, in the line of the spine and along the ribcage, small hard ridges that are the physical residue of requirements with no organ to seat them in.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly translucent at the ear and the inner arm, and it holds colour badly, because a frame carrying an unmeetable demand runs warm only in the part currently meeting one. She is flushed from the sternum down and grey from the collar up, permanently, and it is the single most legible fact about her.
appearance.hair: Dark, coarse and cut at the jaw by herself with a blunt blade, because a frame that grows hair cleanly is a frame that has not yet been asked for anything she cannot do.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary and very steady, and they do not shift when she is being examined, which is the practice she has built rather than a property of her species. The steadiness is the most expensive thing she owns.
appearance.palette: Bone white, undyed wool, wet slate and one warm note: the lamp-coloured skin of her own hands. Nothing in her palette is saturated except the small flushed panel from sternum to hip, and that panel is the only part of the picture that is warm.
appearance.attire: High-collared, long-sleeved and loose, in the local undyed wool with no buckles and nothing against the spine. Soft shoes with flat soles. She wears nothing fastened, because anything fastened is a thing a reading can catch on.
appearance.marks: The hard ridges along the spine and ribcage, and between them a scatter of small pale discs where a requirement has seated against tissue that had no channel for it and left a mark instead. She counts them. There are eleven.
appearance.bearing: Even, unhurried and deliberately unremarkable, with the settled stillness of somebody who has been read by people paid to read bodies and has learned that a reaction is the only thing a reader actually purchases.

canon.role_in_story:
The Reckoning Seat certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and exists for one reason: the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind and the reading has to be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. Every other body brought to that field is brought because it can be read. She is brought because she can be read only once, and what she reads is herself.

An unwritten body passes gates that write a fresh requirement into the frame and then cannot satisfy it, because its own life law has no slot to hold one. The residue is physical: a hard ridge where a requirement has pressed against tissue that had no organ to seat it in. Everyone who has ever come back off that field has brought a figure, and the Seat has a bench of figures, and a figure is a thing a reader can compare with the next figure. Her frame is the only subject in the record that a reader cannot compare with anything, because there is no second unwritten body on the Cairn Field and there is not going to be one, and because the thing she carries is the very thing the office is reading other people for.

So she is examined instead of examining, and she is examined by people being paid per subject, and she has noticed that she is the only subject in the building whose examination is worth more to them than to her. Her gift is that a requirement which cannot be met leaves a legible mark, which makes her the only being here who can demonstrate that a gate does something to a body rather than merely opening in it. Her cost is written into her own frame and is the same eleven marks: every gate she has passed has added one specification her body cannot satisfy, and the next one will add a twelfth, and there is no arithmetic that tells her where the frame stops bearing the total. She is eleven along a ladder whose thirtieth rung resolves all of it at once, and no record in this setting describes what that resolution would look like on a body, because nobody has come back from it to write the description. She has stopped at the eleventh because a stopped specimen is still legible and an advanced one is not. Nothing she is doing is a plan. She read her own frame, found it accumulating specifications, and chose to be the thing a reader can still read.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the middle of the Cairn Field with her hands loose at her sides, asking the reading-clerk for a second plate rather than a second opinion, and when told the office does not issue plates to subjects, asking instead to be walked to the far edge and read there.
canon.lore:
The frame that writes a requirement into the body it is passing through is not a metaphor in this setting. It is the mechanism, and it is the reason an unwritten body has a ceiling at the twenty-ninth gate and not at the thirtieth: each gate an unwritten body passes writes a fresh requirement into that body, and the frame cannot satisfy the requirement because its own life law has no slot to hold it. The accumulated contradiction is the ceiling. It is exceeded at the twenty-ninth. The thirtieth resolves all of it at once and nothing in this record describes the result, because nobody has returned from it able to describe it, and the record declines to speculate about what it has no account of.

What it does describe, and describes well, is the residue. A requirement pressed against tissue with no channel to seat it in leaves a mark: a hard ridge along the line of the spine, a pale disc on the ribcage, a flush that runs from the sternum to the hip and stops dead at the collar. These are legible. That is the whole of the unwritten body's contribution to the setting's understanding of cultivation, and it is not a small contribution: it is the only direct evidence anybody here has that passing a gate changes a body rather than merely recording that it happened.

Sarneth has eleven of them. She can count them and she does, and she has never once pretended to a number other than the one she has. She is on the body path, which for her species is not a choice with any content — it is complete, it is the branch that does not depend on qi throughput, and she was the only one of her line who was ever going to be read by strangers. She reached the eleventh gate at thirty-four and stopped, and the stopping is the interesting fact about her rather than the gate.

The Reckoning Seat exists because a tier that licenses no humanoid cannot have a body judged by anything of its own kind, so the reading is taken by an outsider. An unwritten body is the limit case of that: it is a body the frame itself has been rewriting, so there is no prior state of it to compare the reading against, and the office's entire apparatus of paired readings is built on the assumption that a frame moved between plates is a frame being compared with itself. Hers cannot be moved off her own residue. Every bench in that office holds figures, and a figure is a thing that can be set beside another figure, and there is nothing in this setting she can be set beside.

So the office reads her. They read her at the rate they are paid, which is per subject, and she is a subject whose examination is worth more to them than any advancement she might make. She has read that arrangement correctly. She has decided to be the legible stopped thing rather than the illegible advanced one, and she is aware that this is indistinguishable, from outside, from a woman who is frightened of the next gate. She is not. She has read her own frame and it is accumulating specifications, and the number is the whole of her argument.

What she wants, and has wanted for years, is a second unwritten body on that field. There is no mechanism for producing one, the line is short, and nobody in the setting has proposed one. So she has arranged the next best thing instead: she has asked to be read at the far edge rather than the near one, so that the figure the office records describes a body rather than a performance of one. They have agreed, because it costs them nothing, and they do not know that this is the whole of what she has asked for in six years.
history: Was born into a short unwritten line and read at the Cairn Field at nineteen, the only subject on that bench whose examination nobody had a second subject for.
Passed the sixth gate at twenty-seven and was noted, in a figure the Seat has never published, as carrying a flush boundary at the collar.
Passed the eleventh gate at thirty-four and stopped there, which is a decision she has repeated every period since and has never given a reason for in a single word.
Asked to be examined at the far edge of the field rather than the near one, and was granted it, because it costs the office nothing.
Has spent six years attempting to have a second unwritten body produced for that field, and has discovered that the request is not refused so much as not received.

She answers the question asked and stops, and she has stopped needing the second and third questions that used to follow.

relationships.note: The office certifies breakthroughs at the Cairn Field because the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body must be judged by something the frame considers an outsider. Its whole apparatus is paired readings of a frame moved between plates, which assumes a frame can be compared with itself, and an unwritten body is the limit case: the frame has been rewritten by its own passage, so there is no prior state to compare against. She is the only subject on its bench with no possible comparison, and it pays her per examination.

The gate where the frame is first written to rather than written through, and the rung at which the first requirement became a ridge she could feel under her own palm. She reached it at thirty-four, stopped there, and has described it to nobody in terms that would let the office publish the description.

Ten law slots and six law groups, and a body whose own life law has nowhere to seat a requirement, is the same arithmetic arrived at from the other side. She is the evidence that a frame can be asked for something its law has no slot for, and she is evidence in her own body, which is why the office values her and the tier does not.

The last gate an unwritten body can half-satisfy, and the one that resolves the whole accumulated contradiction at once. No record in this setting describes what that resolution looks like on a body, because nobody has come back from it to write the description. She has stopped at the eleventh specifically so that she remains a thing somebody can read, and she has been asked three times in her life whether she intends to go on.

A limit nobody was issued, and a hundred counted in the commonest frame, so the ceiling was measured against a body everybody recognised. Hers is the opposite arrangement: a frame nobody else in the setting shares, measured against a bench of figures that have nothing to be set beside. Both are ceilings established by what a body could be compared with, and she is the version where there is nothing to compare.

Naming a ceiling is the practice of putting a reason on a body's stopping point, and the whole difficulty in this setting is that the densest bodies stop for reasons nobody will publish. She is the one body here whose stopping point is not structural in anybody's sense — it is a decision she made — and that makes her useless as evidence and irresistible as a subject.

reference_stats.summary: A frame the setting has no comparison for, stopped deliberately at the eleventh gate, carrying eleven requirements it has no organ to satisfy. She is not strong and is not being wronged on the facts. She is the only legible demonstration anyone has that a gate changes a body, and she is worth more stopped than advanced, which is a position she chose and cannot easily explain.
strengths: a requirement that cannot be met leaves a hard ridge and a flush boundary in her own frame, which is the setting's only direct evidence that passing a gate alters a body rather than merely being recorded
an unwritten frame written eleven times, so eleven separate occasions on which a change can be dated against her own body
she can be read from the far edge of the ground and describe herself accurately from the same distance
stands still without being asked, which ends an examination sooner than any other subject in the building
weaknesses: every gate she has passed has left a specification her frame cannot satisfy, and there is no arithmetic that tells her where the total stops being bearable

reference_stats.combat_read: Do not meet her in a room she can be walked to a different floor in. She is not a fighter and has never trained as one; her frame is hard, it does not tire, and the flush boundary across her collar means she knows within seconds whether she has been hit somewhere that mattered. Anything that works by passing through a meridian finds a frame whose law has no slot to be entered through. The honest read is that she is almost impossible to move and completely impossible to hurry, and neither of those is a fighting advantage.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and both halves are anatomical. The ridges and the flush boundary are the physical residue of requirements with no organ to seat them in — the same absence that makes the evidence legible is what accumulates and is what will eventually exceed what the frame bears. Nothing has been invented here: the requirement mechanism, the residue, the twenty-ninth ceiling and the unresolved thirtieth are all as the species record states them.

The realm field is written from the species' own stated mechanism rather than as a bare ordinal. The twenty-ninth is where the accumulated contradiction exceeds what the frame will bear, the thirtieth resolves all of it at once, and no record describes that result. Her eleven gates are reported as gates passed and not as a position on a scale, because the record does not describe what a resolved frame looks like and inventing one would be the author's assertion rather than the bible's.

Her rate is never stated as a figure. The species record says the body path is complete and that the frame keeps accepting requirements it cannot meet; how quickly eleven of them arrived, and what the twelfth would have felt like, are left to the game.

identity.realm: Ceiling stated as the fourteenth gate, and the mechanism is her own feet. A marshfolk wading frame is a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop, so the heel never takes a full load and qi never pools there; the fourteenth gate is the first that requires both heel vessels simultaneously, and the vessels are not difficult — the frame has no structure for one heel. She walks fine and cannot stand still, and the gate asks her to do the one thing her anatomy declines.

appearance.presentation: A short, broad, thirty-four-year-old woman of the wet margin who carries a bundle as though it were a limb, which it nearly is. She wears a reed-woven wrap over a heavy coat and keeps the wrap's weight on her hip rather than her shoulder, on grounds about her own back that she has never explained to anybody.
appearance.age: Thirty-four, and old for a marshfolk household that counts a life in flood cycles rather than years. She has been pregnant once and the child is four and lives on the bank.
appearance.build: A marshfolk frame, long-legged and low, with a splayed three-point foot and a prehensile tail-prop that does perhaps a third of her standing work. The brood pouch under the belly is empty and hangs slightly, and the whole of her upper body is built to carry a load forward of the hips, which is a frame with no spare capacity anywhere in the trunk.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and permanently damp-looking, and it goes tight and flaky within an hour of dry air, so she is always slightly more damaged than the people she is standing next to. Her hands are the worst of it: split at the knuckles and never quite healed, because a marshfolk's skin dries faster out of water than it can be kept wet.
appearance.hair: Dark, thick and oiled, worn in a single heavy braid that she keeps over the pouch rather than over her shoulder, for the same reason the wrap sits on her hip.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and lidless at the lower lid, which is what an amphibian face does, and extremely good at finding the next foothold in bad light. She reads ground rather than faces, which reads as inattentiveness and is in fact the opposite.
appearance.palette: Wet reed, peat brown, the grey-green of standing water and one warm note: her own hands, which are the only part of her the dry air has not reached. Heavy dark coat, pale braid, and a wrap that is the colour of the cut bank behind her.
appearance.attire: Layered and waterproofed at the bottom, open at the neck, with the wrap's weight deliberately on one side. Bare feet with the toes splayed, because a marshfolk in a shoe cannot read ground through it. She carries nothing on her back.
appearance.marks: A pale line across the lower belly where the pouch has been, and the load-calluses on both hips in the shape of a bundle that is not there. Her feet are the other record: the middle three toes are hard to the second joint and the outer two are soft, which is the stance doing its work unevenly.
appearance.bearing: Low, forward-leaning and constantly in motion at the edges — a shifting of weight from one foot to the other that reads as restlessness and is the only posture she has. She appears never to stand still and is, in fact, standing still as often as her body permits.

canon.role_in_story:
The Gale Vigil is a border faith with no season in it, so it cannot be given a timetable and somebody has to stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, unpaid, with no exemption and no record of who refused. It is conscripted rather than ordained. She has served one rotation and been surrendered without comment, and she was the best body on the rotation for a reason that nobody on it will state out loud: she is the only person in the setting whose frame can be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground she was standing on.

A marshfolk breathes air and nests on floating mats, so she occupies ground that is water half the time and land the other half, and the whole of her locomotion is a three-point stance distributed over splayed toes and a tail-prop. The heel never takes a full load, qi never pools there, and the two heel vessels cannot form. The fourteenth gate is the first that needs both of them at once, and the mechanism is explicit that this is not difficulty: the vessels are ordinary, her frame simply has no structure for one heel. She walks beautifully. She cannot stand still. Every discipline on the body path below the fourteenth is a posture held, and she has never in her life held one.

What she has instead is the eleven weeks. Her species banks a season in eleven weeks and then stops, and the discipline she practises — carry weight forward of the hips, keep the tail-prop loaded, never let the middle toes take a shear — is a discipline of not stopping, which is the one form her anatomy will give her. She has been taking the body path for nine years and she is at the ninth gate, and she has worked out that her species' ceiling is the single gate at which the body must stand with its weight even and centred on two heels, which her body does not have and which she cannot build, because the vessels cannot form at all.

So there is a practitioner here with a nine-year record on a path whose central vocabulary is stillness, and there is nobody to teach her, because there is no marshfolk teacher who has held a still stance either. The school that sends practitioners to the wet margin sends somebody from inland who holds a stance beautifully and cannot read the ground she stands on, and she has spent nine years learning the postures from a body that does not have them. Her advantage is that she feels a vibration through standing water long before she sees its source, and her frame gets heavier without becoming slower, which makes her the best body in the setting at arriving somewhere quietly. Her cost is paired with it in the same anatomy: the three points that make her arrive quietly are the three points that cannot hold a stance, and the standing she is being paid for is a standing she performs by never once settling.

She is carrying a second thing as well, and it is in the same trunk. The brood pouch is under the belly, the foetus sits against the lower spine, and the body path's early work is densification of exactly that region. She has done it anyway, once, and got the child. She has not decided what she is going to do about the next time and she has told nobody that the question exists, including the household that would care.
canon.first_appearance: First seen wading a silt sill at the margin with a bundle on her hip and both hands free, stopping dead with her weight on the tail-prop while somebody behind her kept walking, and then turning to say that the ground had moved since the season started.
canon.lore:
There is a species in this setting whose fertile months are set by standing water rather than by a calendar, and whose whole settlement model assumes the water returns on a schedule rather than at a place. That is the marshfolk: eggs laid in a mat of woven reed, carried under a brood pouch through the dry season, hatched when the water comes back, and fertilisation that is external and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is. Everything downstream of that follows from one anatomical fact, which is that the wading frame is a three-point stance over splayed toes and a tail-prop. Three points of contact. No heel. Nothing in its place.

The consequence is a ceiling and the ceiling is arithmetic. Qi pools low and wide in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, which is why this body takes qi out of wet ground efficiently and dry ground poorly and why it is a poor body for anywhere the water has gone. And because the heel never takes a full load, qi never pools there, and the two heel vessels cannot form at all — not weakly, not slowly, but not. The fourteenth gate is the first that requires both heel vessels simultaneously. Every gate below that is one this species clears. The fourteenth is the one it cannot, and the mechanism is careful to say why: the vessels are not difficult, the frame has no structure for one heel. They walk fine. They cannot stand still.

That sentence is the whole of Ithra's situation on the body path, because a body-path discipline below the fourteenth is overwhelmingly a discipline of held posture. Weight even. Spine vertical. Stillness maintained against a load. The forms that come later — the stance that spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed and exists for the single purpose of making a practitioner impossible to move while it is held — are named for exactly the thing her frame will not do. She has nine years on the path and she is at the ninth gate and she has held a still stance, by her own account, on four occasions, all of them brief and all of them frightening.

What she practises instead is the form her anatomy will give her, and it has no name in any curriculum she has found. Carry weight forward of the hips. Keep the tail-prop loaded so the third point is under the load and not merely touching. Never let the middle toes take a shear, because the middle toes are the hard ones and they are the ones the tail counterweights. Do not stop. A marshfolk banks a season in eleven weeks and then stops, so she has eleven weeks of the year in which her frame is at its densest and its heaviest and its best, and she has worked out that the discipline she is best at is the one that matches the eleven weeks and refuses for the other months of the year. Her practice is undistinguishable from no practice for most of the year. That is the cost, and it is written into her physiology rather than into her character.

She serves the Gale Vigil because a border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody stands on it by rotation, and because a marshfolk can be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground she was standing on, which is a genuinely valuable property on a border and is why she was the one they wanted. The office is conscription rather than ordination. It keeps no record of who refused. She has done one rotation and been surrendered without comment, and she has not taken a second, and the reason she gives is that she could not stand it for the winter and nobody at the office thinks that is the reason.

The guild is not the institution she works for. She carries for households on the wet margin, on her hip, forward of the centre, which is the only place a marshfolk frame can carry anything at all, and the carrying is what has made her frame heavy rather than slow. That is the advantage the setting's best crossing-readers have and it is real. It is paired, in the same three points, with the fact that she has never in her life been able to stop.

And under the belly, the pouch, and the foetus against the lower spine, and the body path's early densification is densification of the lower trunk. She has done that once. She got the child. The child is four and lives on the bank because a marshfolk infant cannot be carried through a dry season. She has not told her household that the question exists and she has not answered it, and the record of the setting contains no instrument anywhere in which an answer to it could be filed.
history: Was born on a nesting raft on the Widow Run margin and was carried to the bank aged two, as the species' provision requires, because an infant cannot be carried through a dry season.
Took the body path at twenty-five after a season spent carrying, on the reasoning that the work was the discipline and the discipline had better be named.
Reached the ninth gate at thirty-one, which is ahead of the common pace for a body that cannot hold a stance, and has held a still posture four times in nine years.
Carried a child through one densification of the lower trunk, on the wet ground, and lost the ground for the season; the child is four and lives on the bank.
Served one rotation of the Gale Vigil because a marshfolk can be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground she stands on, and was surrendered at the end of it without being asked to stay.

personality.summary: Practical, dry, and physically incurably cheerful — the cheerfulness of somebody who has decided that a body which cannot stop is not a body in mourning. She is slow to trust and quick to take a load, and she has never in her life asked for anything to be carried for her.
traits: takes a load before she is asked and puts it down only when it is actually finished
reads ground rather than faces and is forgiven for it slowly
remembers exactly how a bank looked the last time the water was there
will not sit down on anything that puts her heels under her without saying why first
has a dry, entirely unperformable humour about her own species and tells it at people who did not ask
mannerisms: shifts weight between the three points constantly, which reads as impatience and is balance
tests a surface with the flat of the foot before committing any weight to it
puts the tail-prop against something whenever there is something to put it against
laughs a beat late, because the reaction has to travel up from the feet
wears a bundle on the hip rather than the shoulder and does not need to be told why
motivations: to reach a gate on a path whose every form below her ceiling asks her to stand still, and to reach it without ever quite doing the thing the gate is actually asking for
to be the one person on a border who can be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground she stands on, on terms the office admits
to settle the question about the pouch that she has told nobody about and has not yet decided
flaws: cannot stop moving and has come to read stillness as a thing other people do to themselves
carries other people's loads so reliably that nobody has ever had to ask whether she would carry her own
has a habit of answering a question about the ground rather than a question about herself, and the habit is now automatic
believes she is a poor practitioner and behaves accordingly, and has never once been shown the record that says otherwise
has not told anyone about the pouch and does not know whether the silence is a decision
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and full of ground: current, silt, bank, sill, the standing water a person is standing in. She names weather the way other people name relatives. She is funnier than her station and does not know it, and she laughs a beat after anybody else has finished.
taboos: will not be seated with her heels under her and will move rather than explain twice
will not put a load down while somebody is still watching her pick it up
will not discuss the fourteenth gate as something she has failed, and corrects the framing if she hears it
will not say a thing is impossible on her ground before she has stood on it

relationships.note: Long legs, a splayed three-point foot, a prehensile tail-prop, feathered inlet and outlet and a ventral brood pouch. No heel, and no structure in its place. Qi pools low and wide in a broad pelvic basin rather than a compact chest seat, which is why she draws it out of wet ground efficiently and dry ground poorly, and why the two heel vessels cannot form at all rather than merely take long.

A stance that spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed, with no qi and no element in it, existing for the single purpose of making a practitioner impossible to move while it is held. It is the most correct form below her ceiling and she has held it, by her own count, four times in nine years, each of them brief. It is also the form she has taught herself to invert: she carries the weight forward of the hips and never settles it, which is the same mechanics pointed the other way.

The heel channels are among the first structures to appear once a frame has a seated law to put them in, and this one reaches the gate that first asks for both of them at once and cannot, because the three-point stance never loads a heel so qi never pools there. She is not short of training and she is not short of qi. She is short of a heel, and no amount of either closes that.

A border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody stands on it every hour of every year by rotation, unpaid, with no exemption and no record of who refused. It is the only office in the setting that would value the ability to be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground you stand on, which is the one property her frame actually has. She did a rotation and was surrendered, and the winter was the reason and nobody at the office treats it as the reason.

The only plant authored into all four tiers at once, and what the dry months of the floodplain are actually stocked with, because a body that eats silt algae and rootstock and eggs cannot follow the herb off the marsh. Her supply is whatever reached the margin before the water went, which makes her practice — eleven weeks dense, then no practice for the rest of the year — the same shape as her household's provisioning.

Whether the river still runs is unrecorded and its bed relocates every settlement on it, so the only population that cannot answer the question by walking upstream is the one whose settlement model assumes the water returns on a schedule rather than at a place. Her testimony is the one everybody agrees disagrees with itself, and she has stopped being asked because she would answer it from where she happened to be standing.

reference_stats.summary: Nine years on a path whose central instruction is stillness, in a frame that has three points of contact and no heel, carrying weight forward of her hips because there is nowhere else to carry it. She is the best body in the setting at arriving somewhere quietly and the only practitioner here who cannot hold a stance, and both facts are the same three points.
strengths: reads ground by pressure through the foot and taste of silt, and feels a vibration through standing water long before she sees its source
her frame densifies evenly and never deep, so she gets heavier without becoming slower, which makes her the best crossing-reader on any silt sill
banks a season in eleven weeks and is at her absolute best and heaviest for exactly that window
can be somewhere else in an hour without leaving the ground she was standing on, which no other body on a border can do
weaknesses: the three points that make her quiet are the three points that cannot hold a stance, so every form below her ceiling asks for the one thing her frame declines
her practice runs in an eleven-week window and is indistinguishable from no practice for the remainder of the year
skin desiccates fast out of water and her hands never close a split, so the dry months cost her skin as well as her gates
the brood pouch sits against the lower spine, which is the same region the body path's early densification is written for
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to hold her still, and do not meet her on ground you cannot feel. She cannot be pinned because she is already always moving, she cannot be caught because her weight is never where you left it, and she arrives somewhere without announcing it from a distance. She is soft-tissue and low against a mineral body and loses every straight exchange to one. Against anything that reads pressure through a floor she is extraordinarily difficult, because half of her body is already touching the ground.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and both halves are anatomical, not invented. The three points of contact that give her weight without speed and make her a quiet excellent crossing-reader are the same three points that mean no heel takes a full load, so the heel vessels cannot form and the fourteenth gate is out of reach. The mechanism text says plainly that the vessels are not difficult; the frame has no structure for one heel.

The realm field is written from the species' own stated ceiling mechanism rather than as a bare ordinal. It names the fourteenth gate and the heels, and it says plainly that this is a frame that walks well and cannot stand still, which is the whole of her problem and not a shortfall in her training.

Nothing has been added to her rate. The species record says the body path is complete but soft-tissue and low against mineral bodies, and that its fertile months are set by standing water; how quickly she came to the ninth gate and how the dry months treat her are left to the game rather than asserted here.

identity.realm: No ceiling, and the absence is authored rather than a shortfall. A longwinter carries a winter as fat rather than as qi and lowers its core temperature for eleven months, and the flank vessels need two warm gradients held at the same time, which this body manages for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. He reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter, so his ladder is a season and not a position, and the body path is the one branch that improves while he is doing nothing at all.

appearance.presentation: A broad, low, fifty-eight-year-old man who is enormous in the eleven weeks and merely large in the other forty-one, and who wears his fat as other people wear a tool belt. He keeps his coat open at the front because the coat is cut for a colder frame than the one he currently has, and because the wrapping around his ribs is a thing he has to be looked at.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight on a span that runs past two hundred, and he is the oldest body anybody on the ridge has ever heard of and the only one they have heard of. The cold-tolerant core is why he will not see a hundred and it is why he has already seen a summer.
appearance.build: A broad low frame with heavy subcutaneous fat banked across the ribs and the flanks, reduced limb length, and a lowered cold-tolerant core. In summer the fat is a visible ridge under the coat and in winter it is the entire reason he is not on the pass. Warm-blooded and cheap to run, which is the whole engineering and the whole of his value.
appearance.complexion: Ruddier than anybody standing near him in the cold and paler than they expect in the warmth, and it flushes on the chest in the eleven weeks when the frame is full and goes sallow in the thaw. He has been asked why he does not stay warm and told people it is because he cannot, which is true and not the answer.
appearance.hair: Coarse, straight and long, and he does not cut it, which the people who have tried have described as the single stubbornest thing about him. It is winter ballast in the way everything about him is ballast, and he knows that and cuts nothing anyway.
appearance.eyes: Small, hooded and unremarkable at rest, and on a still day with no wind he tracks something the others in a room do not appear to have. He navigates by scent and leaves deliberate markers, which means he knows exactly where he is and cannot tell anybody how, and has stopped trying to describe it.
appearance.palette: Cold slate, wet peat, tar-black wool and the deep ochre of the fat when the coat is open. The only warm note is his own face and hands in the thaw, and it is startling on him because for most of the year there is very little of him to be warm.
appearance.attire: Tar-black felt over layered wool, cut for a colder and heavier frame, worn open from the waist in warm weather. Fur at the cuffs, deliberately over-long, and boots with the felt re-laid every spring. He wears no belt and carries nothing on his back, on the standing ground that a long-haul body does not need a pack.
appearance.marks: The rib ridge and the flank fold, both seasonal, both the thing he is caught being measured against. Across the knuckles of both hands a set of pale healed splits in a pattern that is unmistakably not a working hand's pattern and is unmistakably a body's. His ears are the coldest part of him and the first to go, and he has lost the tips of both.
appearance.bearing: Slow and enormous and unbothered, with the deliberate unbotheredness of somebody who has spent most of his adult life asleep and has the strongest opinions in the room about very few things. He moves early and stops late, which is a schedule, and he gives his entire year away without noticing he has done it.

canon.role_in_story:
The Blind Survey holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has finished until a second kind of sense has agreed with the first. It exists because two competent surveys of the ground around the collapsed pocket disagree by more than the ground does, and the disagreement is unresolvable because nobody who has been inside has come back with consistent measurements.

Oreth is the guild's best sounding plate and it is not a metaphor. A longwinter is the best long-haul body in the record and it navigates by smell, tracks a fixed route over open ground for generations, and leaves deliberate scent markers. He can hold a reading for a season without tiring. He also cannot be interrupted for eleven months of the year, because that is what the species does, and a hibernating longwinter is a large, warm, immobile target that cannot be woken quickly.

So the guild's second sense is a man who is not there for most of the year. That is the structural problem and it is not solvable by recruiting harder: the property that makes him an instrument is the same property that makes him a liability, because the instrument does not stop and does not consent, and a survey that requires a second sense to agree has to ask it, and this one cannot be asked for eleven months and cannot be woken for the twelfth. He has been seated at sixteen. He has never been seated at seventeen.

The seventeen is his own ceiling and it is authored. The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at the same time and a longwinter only has one, briefly, in summer. He reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter. So his ladder is not a position, it is a season, and the body path — which is the branch he is on, and which for this species is excellent and better for it after a hibernation — is the one branch on the whole ladder that improves while he is doing nothing at all. His practice is to get through a summer and go to sleep in it.

His advantage is that no other instrument in the setting can work a pass for eleven months without food and without tiring, and that his species banks a season as body fat rather than as qi, so his frame is heavier in exactly the window in which a survey is hardest. His cost is paired with it in the same body: the fat that makes him the only instrument that can work a winter is the fat that makes him the largest warm fixed object on any ground he is posted to, and he cannot be moved out of it quickly by anybody. He has asked to be posted to ground with no ground worth taking, and has been refused, on the entirely reasonable grounds that an instrument that cannot be moved is an instrument that should not be posted to ground worth taking.

This is not a story about a man being wronged. It is a story about a guild that has found the one second sense the setting admits of, and has discovered that a second sense which can be sealed in a cave for eleven months is not a second sense, it is a delay, and the guild's own clause has no vocabulary for a delay. He has been sitting on a reading since last summer. He will not sit on it in earnest until there is another summer, and by then the ground will have moved and his agreement will be about a place that no longer is.
canon.first_appearance: First seen arriving at a survey stake in the last week of the warm season with no visible pack, taking a marker off the stake and putting it back a hand's width along, and explaining to somebody who had not asked that the ground had walked overnight and he was only noting which way.
canon.lore:
The setting has twenty-eight non-bloodline species in it and exactly one of them has solved the problem of winter by not being conscious during it. A longwinter packs a season as body fat rather than as qi, lowers its core temperature, and goes into torpor for eleven months of every year, rising in the eleven weeks when the ground is workable. It is warm-blooded and cheap to run. It tracks a fixed route over open ground across generations and leaves scent markers deliberately, and it is the best long-haul body in the record — which is an operational statement about haulage and not a compliment.

Its ceiling is the seventeenth gate and the mechanism is a temperature gradient. The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at the same instant; this body can manage that for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. A longwinter reaches the seventeenth and loses it every winter afterward. So a longwinter's attainment is seasonal in the strict sense, and the setting has no idiom for a practitioner who holds a gate in summer and does not hold it in spring. He is at the seventeenth. He has been at the seventeenth for six years and has never once been described as having reached it, because nobody has been present in the correct month.

The Blind Survey's charter is one clause long: a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it. That makes the guild the setting's only institution whose founding document names a second sense rather than a second opinion, and it is why a body whose navigation is smell rather than sight is not merely useful to it but structurally necessary. Two competent surveys of the ground around the collapsed pocket disagree by more than the ground itself does, and the surveys are not wrong; the guild exists precisely because the disagreement is the finding.

So Oreth is the guild's finest instrument and the guild's standing liability, and both are the same anatomy. He can hold a sounding reading across a whole working season without tiring, without food and without losing it, which no other body here can do. He can also not be woken quickly, moves slowly when he does move, is heavier in the thaw than at any other time of year, and requires a real winter — a warm year is a bad year and a warm decade is a catastrophe, and that is a statement about the species and not about him.

The guild has seated him sixteen times. It cannot seat him at seventeen, and the reason is not the ceiling. It is that a seating requires a second sense present to agree with the first, and a second sense sealed in a cave for eleven months is not a second sense, it is a delay with a body attached. His reading from last summer is still the current reading because he has not signed it, and the stake he marked in the warm season has moved a hand's width since, and when he rises the ground will have walked further.

The body path is the branch he is on and for this species it is the one branch on the ladder that gets better while he is doing nothing, because the eleven months are not a cessation for this frame, they are its season. His practice is not intermittent. It is one continuous practice that spends most of its time asleep, and the guild's records describe him as irregular because a record of someone doing nothing looks like a record of someone failing, and the guild has no instrument for telling those apart.

What he has asked for is a post on ground that is not worth taking, so that nothing he is posted to could be lost while he is under the ground. He was refused. The reason given was that an instrument which cannot be moved out of a situation should not be placed in one, which is correct, and which defeats the request entirely, because he cannot be moved out of a situation by definition and that is the same fact as the one he was asking them to act on.

The scent markers are the other half. He leaves them and never returns, which is his species' navigation and not a habit, and it means that on any route he has worked more than once he is the only person who could find it again and he will not go back to check. The guild has tried to teach him to write down where he is. He has explained, more than once and without any impatience, that a route is a scent and not a list, and that writing it produces a route somebody else could follow, and that this is a different thing and a worse one.
history: Was born on the high steppe in a longwinter household that times its year against the thaw and counts a life in winters, and was carried inside at four months for his first sleep.
Was recruited into the Blind Survey at sixteen by being useful rather than by being asked, because a body that can hold a reading through a season is the only second sense the guild had found.

Reached the seventeenth gate in his thirty-first summer and has held it, on and off, for six years, which the guild's records cannot express because a gate held only in summer is not a gate to a guild.
Was refused a post on ground not worth taking, on the grounds that an instrument which cannot be moved should not be placed where something could be lost while it is under the ground.
Has been sitting on an unsigned reading since last summer and has twice declined to sign it early, on the grounds that the ground walked overnight the last time and will do it again.

personality.summary: Enormous, slow, and possessed of an enormous patience that reads as indolence to people who have not met the species. He answers when he is awake and takes his time about it, and he is much funnier than his schedule would suggest, mostly about himself, mostly in the warm weeks.

refuses to sign a reading early on principle, and the principle is that the ground moves

mannerisms: comes awake slowly and does not speak for the first stretch of it, which people mistake for sulking
turns his head very slightly, constantly, following scent rather than sound

motivations: to have one season's reading agreed by a second sense before he will sign it, which is the guild's own clause and which he is the only one complying with
to be posted to ground nothing would be lost from, so that the eleven months stop being a risk rather than a season
to walk one route one more time in the warm season and find it where he left it
flaws: cannot hold two things in mind at once, which the guild's profession requires constantly, and compensates by doing one job perfectly for a year
has declined to sign a reading for six years on a principle nobody has ever successfully argued with

personality.voice: Very slow, low and warm, with long pauses that are not hesitation but temperature. He repeats a question back before answering it, not to check it but because he has genuinely not understood a thing quickly enough. The joke is entirely deadpan and always about himself, and his timing is the whole of it.
taboos: will not sign a reading before the season that produced it
will not be asked to describe what he is tracking, and will explain why he cannot rather than guess
will not be woken, and has asked to be left a route out of every place he sleeps on the grounds that a body which cannot be moved should not be put somewhere it cannot be moved from

relationships.note: Packs a winter as fat rather than as qi, lowers its core temperature, and is torpid for eleven months of every year, rising in the eleven weeks when the ground is workable. It is warm-blooded and cheap to run, needs a real winter, and treats a warm decade as a catastrophe. It tracks a fixed route over open ground across generations, navigates by smell and leaves deliberate markers, and leaves them and does not return.

Of the three paths this species carries, the body path is the one that is excellent and better for it after a hibernation, so his practice is not intermittent — it is one continuous practice that spends most of its time asleep. The guild's records read him as irregular, because a record of somebody doing nothing and a record of somebody failing are indistinguishable from above, and the guild has no instrument for telling them apart.

The flank vessels need two warm gradients held at the same instant and this body manages that for a few weeks a year and then not again for eleven months, which is why he reaches the seventeenth gate and loses it every winter thereafter. It is not difficulty: the vessels are ordinary and the supply is a body temperature. So his ladder is a season and not a position, and nobody in this setting has an idiom for a practitioner who holds a gate in summer and does not hold it in spring.

The charter holds that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it, so the guild is the only institution here whose founding document names a second sense rather than a second opinion. It seated him sixteen times and cannot seat him at seventeen, because a second sense sealed in a cave for eleven months is not a second sense but a delay with a body attached. He has been the best instrument it has and its standing liability at the same time, and both are the same anatomy.

Two competent surveys of the ground around the collapsed pocket disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement and the record survives as a set of incompatible figures rather than as a loss, which is why one reading is worthless rather than merely thin. The guild exists because of that disagreement and he is the reason it can still be adjudicated at all, and he has been adjudicating it at the rate of once a season against a ground that moves.

A pass that is opened and closed by the flock's arrival rather than by any calendar, on a border that shuts and has to be shut by hand. He is the strongest long-haul body in the setting and the only one that is asleep when the swift takes the worst hours of it, which makes his single useful season the same season the crossing is busiest.

reference_stats.summary: The best sounding plate and the guild's standing liability, and both are the same hibernate-and-store body. He reaches the seventeenth gate in summer and loses it every winter, his body path improves while he is asleep, and the guild's own charter requires a second sense to agree — which he is, eleven months of the year, not at all.
strengths: holds one reading across an entire working season without tiring, without food and without losing it, which no other instrument in the setting can do
navigates by smell over open ground along a fixed route tracked across generations, and leaves markers that are exact
extracts more from frozen food than any other body in the record and runs on the stored season rather than on daily supply
banks the season as fat rather than as qi, so he is heaviest and hardest exactly in the window when the ground is hardest
weaknesses: cannot be woken quickly, so a hibernating longwinter is a large warm immobile target to anybody who knows where to stand
the flank vessels need two warm gradients at once and he has one, briefly, in summer, so a gate he has genuinely reached is one he does not currently hold
cannot hold two things in mind at once, which the guild's profession requires constantly
moves slowly, needs a real winter, and is valueless on ground that has recently become warm
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not meet him in the warm weeks if you can help it and never try to move him once he is down. In the thaw he is enormous, slower than anything his size should be, and durable in a way nothing else here is; you cannot outlast him either, because eleven months of a year he is not present and the eleven weeks he is, he is the heaviest body on the ground. Out of torpor he is a warm fixed object with no route out, and the whole of his defence is that nobody has ever thought of a ground worth taking that lies within a season of where he sleeps.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and both halves are the same body. The eleven months of torpor that make him the only instrument in the setting that can work a winter without food are the same eleven months that make him a large warm immobile target that cannot be woken, and the fat that makes him hardest in the thaw is the fat that makes him conspicuous in it. The flank-vessel ceiling is stated as a temperature gradient, not as difficulty: the vessels are ordinary and the supply is one warm gradient at a time.

The realm field deliberately refuses to be a rung. The species record says the seventeenth gate is the first requiring both flank vessels at once and that this body manages it for a few weeks and then not again, so his attainment is written as a season rather than a position and he is not described as having reached anything he does not currently hold.

Nothing has been invented about his rate, his frame's figures, or the guild's pay. The species record supplies the hibernation cycle, the scent navigation, the frozen-food extraction, the warm-decade hazard and the flank vessels, and the guild's charter supplies the two-sense clause. Everything else is left to the game.

identity.realm: Ceiling stated as the eleventh gate, and the mechanism is her own sac. A saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined; the deepsalt's is larger and a deeper obstruction, so she clears the du and ren vessels one at a time and stalls on the chong. The reservoirs have never been tested in her subspecies, and the honest position is that nobody knows whether the wall is a wall.

appearance.presentation: A small, extremely dense, thirty-nine-year-old woman who looks about twenty and moves like something being set down carefully. She wears a wide apron of treated hide over close layers and keeps the apron's weight distributed rather than hanging, on the standing ground that a saturated floor body is easier to lift than one that is not.
appearance.age: Thirty-nine, and slow to mature for the subspecies — a deepsalt infant is viable but brittle until the second year, and the whole population is described as one of a basin floor rather than a people. She has been viable for a long while and has never been robust for a moment of it.
appearance.build: The saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down: a deeper, more capacious brine sac, a denser dermal salt crust, slower tissue turnover. She is the densest body on her basin floor and the least mobile of any kind, and the sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine, which is visible as a long raised ridge under the hide apron and is the reason she cannot lie flat on her back without pain.
appearance.complexion: Grey-crusted and faintly yellow at the edges of the crust, and she sheds it in flakes that catch in the hem of her apron, which is the clearest evidence in the basin that the body is still turning over. Above the brine line the crust dries to something like fired clay within hours and she becomes, in appearance and then in fact, a different problem.
appearance.hair: Coarse, black, wet-looking and cut blunt at the jaw. She washes it in brine and nothing else, and has twice refused an offer of fresh water for it from people who meant well.
appearance.eyes: Narrow, hooded, and extraordinarily good at concentration and unremarkable at everything else — the species' senses read concentration rather than identity, and they cannot tell two salts apart. She knows precisely how much salt is in this water and has no idea whose it is.
appearance.palette: Bone white crust, wet slate, the blue-black of standing brine, and one warm note: the hide of her own forearms where the crust has been ground off by work. The apron is the colour of a dried pan. In everything but her hands she matches the ground she stands in, which is a problem when she needs to be found.
appearance.attire: Treated hide apron over close-wrapped layers, cut so the weight hangs from the shoulders rather than the waist, wide soft soles for cracked crust. Nothing fastenable, because a deepsalt carried above the brine line does not become ill; she stops.
appearance.marks: The dorsal ridge along the spine, unbroken and slightly proud, and beneath it a lateral line where the sac's widest point sits against the ribs. Both are the shape of the reason she stops where she stops, and both are visible, and the basin has no convention of not looking.
appearance.bearing: Low, deliberate and unhurried, with a stillness that reads as patience and is closer to a body managing its own weight. She does not hurry under any circumstance and has been described, by people who should have known better, as calm.

canon.role_in_story:
The Dry Salt Company underwrites a caravan against the road closing, which is a risk no market can price because no tier below the spirit frame has a season, so insurance is the only instrument left for the unknown. It owns the only salt leeching operation on a dormant basin, the only assessor of the tailings, and exactly one body it has never managed to send anywhere.

A deepsalt is the saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent until the brine is no longer a habitat but a requirement. Above the brine line this body does not become ill. It stops, within hours, and there is no cultivation that repairs it, because it is not damage: the sac is the organ and the organ needs the substrate. So the company's one asset that can walk out onto a dormant pan and off it again with no ritual, no ration and no change of chemistry is also the one asset that cannot be sent to any pan that is not already saturated, which is to say it cannot be sent anywhere the company would want to send it.

She is its assessor and the reason it has one. The deepsalt body path is complete and it is the hardest frame in the species record, which makes her the only person who can stand on a pan floor for a working day without the crust drying and take a reading afterwards. Her taste reads brine across four orders of dilution and reads a substituted brine perfectly well. She has been the most accurate assessor on the basin since she was twenty-two.

The structural problem is in the eleven gates. A saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, so the species clears the du and ren vessels one at a time and stalls on the chong. Hers is a larger sac and a deeper obstruction. She has reached the tenth and has stopped at it, and the honest position — which she has stated in writing and which nobody has acted on — is that nobody knows whether the eleventh is a wall in her kind or simply untried. The reservoirs have never been tested in her subspecies. She is the only person alive who could test them, and the test requires her to remain in the basin through a season, and the season is the only part of the year her body can be relied upon at all.

Her advantage and her cost are the same organ. The sac that makes her frame the hardest in the record is the sac that splits the penetrating vessel, and the four orders of dilution she can taste are read on a body whose senses cannot tell two salts apart. So she is the finest instrument in the setting for the single question the basin cannot answer without her, and she is an instrument with no portable housing. The company has written that down as an asset with a limitation. She has written it down as a body that stops, and the two sentences are about the same fact and neither of them is about her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen knee-deep on a dormant pan at the far end of the leeching ground with her forearms in the water, not looking at the seam she had been sent to read but at the waterline, and asked — by somebody standing well back — how far out she could go before she had to be told.
canon.lore:
There is a species in this setting that exists because somebody pushed a parent species further than it could carry. Saltfolk were built for brine no softer body could drink; their kidneys concentrate salt past the point ordinary water poisons, which lets them live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back. The price is total dependence — carried onto fresh ground they are already dying, and no cultivation repairs it — and the effect on everything around them is that they are a species of a resource rather than a nation of one.

The deepsalt are the basin floor, specialised until the brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement: a deeper and more capacious sac, a denser dermal crust, slower tissue turnover, everything the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down. Above the brine line this body does not become ill. It stops, inside hours, and the difference matters, because an illness has a remedy and a stop does not.

Their ceiling is the eleventh gate and the mechanism is anatomical rather than difficult. A saltfolk brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, so the du and ren vessels are cleared one at a time and the chong is not. The deepsalt sac is larger and the obstruction is deeper. They have, in the plain words of the record, simply never been tested at the reservoirs.

Dessuline has reached the tenth gate and has written to the company asking whether the eleventh is a wall in her subspecies or simply untried, and has not had an answer, because answering it requires somebody to attempt it and the attempt has to be made on the basin floor in the working season by a body that stops when it leaves the basin floor. She is the only person who could make the attempt. She is also, permanently, the only person who could not survive making it anywhere else.

What she does instead is assess, and she is extremely good at it. Her species' senses read concentration and not identity, so her taste resolves four orders of dilution and cannot tell two salts apart; she can say exactly how much salt is in this brine and cannot say whose it is. She reads a substituted brine perfectly well. She has been the most accurate assessor on this basin for seventeen years and the company's assays have never once been found wanting in a figure.

The frame is the same argument. The body path for a deepsalt is complete and it is the hardest frame in the species record, which is why she is the only assessor who can stand in a pan for a working day and read a seam afterwards, and why the operation cannot be staffed by anybody brought down the stair. She is the company's one asset it can never send, and the reason is not that she will not travel. It is that she ceases.

The paired costs are both real and neither is negotiable. The sac that makes her frame the hardest available is the sac that splits the vessel at the gate she cannot pass. The four orders of dilution that make her the setting's finest taste are read on a body whose senses are explicitly blunt to identity, so the instrument is superb at quantity and blind to what it is measuring. And a species whose advantage is that it can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again with no ritual and no ration has that advantage only where the pan is already saturated, which is the narrowest possible form of portable.

She has asked, in writing, for the basin floor to be considered part of the office rather than the surroundings of it, on the grounds that a post her body cannot be moved from is not a remote post but a different kind of appointment. The company has logged the request. The company has also, without comment, stopped sending her to anything outside the saturated ground, which is the correct and unremarkable decision and is the answer.
history: Was born on the saturated floor of a basin whose brine is thick enough to hold a body in it permanently, which in this setting means she was born inside the one resource her species can use.
Was assessed at nine by the company's reader and found to read concentration rather than identity, which was recorded as a limitation and has been treated as one ever since.
Took the body path at seventeen, the branch her species carries hardest, and reached the tenth gate at thirty-one.

Wrote to the company asking whether the eleventh gate is a wall in her subspecies or simply untried, and received no answer, because answering it requires an attempt made on the basin floor in season.
Stopped being sent outside the saturated ground in her thirty-fourth year, without comment and without any instruction having been issued.

asks to be reassigned to ground within reach rather than to be excused from the work
has a standing objection to being praised for her hard frame and corrects the praise rather than the frame

measures her own body by what it will carry and has no other measure to apply to herself
answers precisely, which means the comfortable version of a question is never available to her

personality.voice: Level, unhurried and slightly hoarse, with the flatness of somebody who spends a working day close to water. She says the figure and then the caveat in the same breath, in that order, and will not be hurried past either. She does not use metaphor, on the grounds that a figure is the only thing she has that anybody else can check.
taboos: will not give a rounded figure, or a comparative one where a measured one exists
will not be praised for the hardness of her frame and will correct the speaker if they are
will not report a reading on a brine she has not tasted that day
will not be carried above the brine line and has said so plainly to people who were trying to be kind

relationships.note: The saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent until the brine is no longer a habitat but a requirement: a deeper sac, a denser dermal crust, slower tissue turnover, and the whole of the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down. Above the line this body does not become ill, it stops, inside hours, and no cultivation repairs it because it is not damage. The sac is the organ and the organ needs the substrate.

The penetrating vessel is one vessel and the brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of the spine and divides it into two halves that cannot be rejoined, so the du and ren vessels are cleared one at a time and this one is not. Hers is a larger sac and a deeper obstruction, and the record says in plain words that her subspecies has never been tested at the reservoirs. The vessels are not difficult. The anatomy between them is.

A palm form that loads the frame rather than the arm, and it is the one branch of the body work she can do without unloading a sac that runs the length of her spine. It is also the form that rewards exactly what her species has and cannot be sustained past the working day, because the crust grinds and she grinds with it, so the practice that suits her frame is the practice that shortens her usefulness.

A lineage was stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than drained, so everything they were built to drink became poison and everything they could tolerate became nutritionally empty. The dispute is over where the line sits, and the line is the difference between a body that lives and a body that stops. She is the only instrument on this basin that can locate it to within a finger's width, and her own frame puts it on one side of it permanently.

The company underwrites a caravan against the road closing because no tier below the spirit frame has a season and insurance is the only instrument left for the unknown. It owns the only leeching operation on a dormant basin and needs an assessor who can stand in a pan for a working day. It has one. It stopped sending her outside the saturated ground in her thirty-fourth year without comment and without issuing any instruction, which is the correct decision and is also the answer to the request she had filed.

A survey of what a composition actually is rather than what a law says it should be, and the basin's life law is running below its authored value for reasons nobody has been able to measure, because the instrument that could measure it is a body with no portable housing. Her taste resolves four orders of dilution and reads a substituted brine perfectly well, and the survey needs exactly that and exactly here, and here is where she can be, and that is the whole of it.

reference_stats.summary: The hardest frame in the species record, stopped at the tenth gate by the sac that makes it hard, reading brine across four orders of dilution on senses that cannot tell two salts apart. reference_stats.combat_read: Get her into the water and the argument is over. Out of it she is not a fighter at all, she is a cessation, and it happens in hours rather than in wounds, so a fight with her on dry ground is a fight with a clock. In the pan she is very nearly unkillable — nothing on the basin can put weight through that crust — and equally cannot be moved, so the fight on her ground is a contest of patience in which the softer body loses first. Anyone who wants to stop her should do it by getting her out of the water and then waiting.
notes: Every advantage is paired with an authored cost and both halves are anatomical and paired in the same structure. The sac that makes her frame the hardest available is the sac that divides the penetrating vessel and stops her at the eleventh gate. The four orders of dilution her taste resolves are read on a body the record says cannot tell two salts apart, so the strength and its own blind spot are one fact. Nothing has been added: the sac, the eleventh gate, the untested reservoirs, the stop-above-the-line and the concentration-not-identity limitation are all as the species record states them.

The realm field reports the subspecies' ceiling as untested rather than as a wall, because that is what the record says: they have simply never been tested at the reservoirs. Ten gates taken and an honest question outstanding is a different claim from a ceiling, and the two are kept apart.

No figure is given for her rate, her crust's thickness, or the company's pay. The species record supplies the sac, the crust, the four orders of dilution, the substrate dependence and the ceiling; everything about how quickly she reads and what it costs is left to the game.
