identity.realm: Ceiling stated as the seventeenth gate, and the mechanism is one resonator rather than two. A vaultborn draws its qi from a single source — the resonance of the object it is sealed inside — and the flank vessels need two pressures held at the same moment, so they clear the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and lose at the flanks. Not because the vessels are hard. Because the supply is one. The body path is complete and slow, and the frame is not what it is for.

appearance.presentation: A slight, forty-four-year-old man whose outline is wrong and has been wrong his whole life. He is arranged along the seal's inner surfaces rather than grown, so his proportions answer to the plating he last stood on rather than to a skeleton, and he wears the same cut of coat as everybody else in the crypt with the seams let out in three places and taken in in two.
appearance.age: Forty-four on a span measured in the object's cycles, which is the only clock available to him and which nobody in the crypt has ever been able to convert into a year. He is not old for his kind and there is no reliable way for him to know what that means.
appearance.build: Unsettled and under-described, which is not a figure of speech in this species: they are arranged along the object's inner surfaces and take their shape from whatever they are standing on. His frame is narrow, slightly over-shouldered and unreasonably hard, and the only honest statement about it is that it would be different if he had last stood somewhere else.
appearance.complexion: Grey and slightly lit from within by his own luminescence, which is a waste product of the resonance he is answering rather than a faculty he has. It brightens when the object sounds and dims when it does not, and he cannot keep it steady, so his face is legible to the crypt in a way no other body's is.
appearance.hair: Fine, colourless and grown in the direction of the last current, which is not always up. It has never been cut by anyone else and he has cut it himself against a plate with a worn seam.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary, dark and enormously wide-set, because the shape of his skull is the plate he was formed against. They have no light in them and they do not need any: he hears the object, and every sound it makes is legible to him as a position, so he navigates by the seal rather than by light.
appearance.palette: Vault iron, cold stone, the pale blue of his own resonance, and one warm note: a lamp-lit hand on a written page. The crypt is dark and he is the only body in it that is, so every frame that includes him has a small cold light in it that belongs to the architecture.
appearance.attire: The crypt's grey working coat with the seams let where his frame is wider than the coat, heavy boots with the soles worn smooth, and a belt carrying a ledger and a stub of graphite. He wears it indoors and has never worn anything else, on the grounds that there is nothing outside to wear it against.
appearance.marks: A faint seam-line where the plating last set, running across the backs of both hands and visible when he holds them up. Nothing heals on him visibly and nothing scars either; the frame simply keeps the last shape and stops discussing it.
appearance.bearing: Careful, unhurried and slightly out of phase with everybody in a room, because he is listening to a building. He turns his head at sounds nobody else has made yet, and apologises for it, and has apologised for it for so long that the apology has become the thing people hear.

canon.role_in_story:
The Field Registry is a mortuary college and it keeps the burnt list: at a settlement funeral the dead are read as the frame said, not as the village remembers, and the divergence between the two is recorded rather than resolved. It exists because the record of a life is also the record of a gate the person was never issued, and it keeps no second copy, because a second copy would be a second opinion.

It is a woman who holds its second reading. Saveth Orlin has signed every entry in the Storm Crypt for four centuries and has refused her own eleven times, which makes her the only person in that vault whose frame the seal re-cuts on a cycle she cannot certify against. He is the reason she has never been able to close one of her own cases, and he is not a guest of the college: his species' deaths have no bodies at all, so the sealed register is not an accumulation of her failures but a category, and he is its standing reason.

Ithamar is its second reader for the Storm Crypt. She certifies that a frame which came up through a re-form of the seal is the same frame that went down, and the office exists because the seal re-cuts its own population on a cycle while a description belongs to the surface that produced it. He has signed every entry in that vault and has refused his own eleven times.

The structural problem is the seventeen. A vaultborn draws its qi from one resonator — the resonance of the object it is sealed inside — and the flank vessels need two pressures at the same instant, so this species clears the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and loses at the flanks, and the mechanism is explicit that the vessels are not difficult and the supply is single. He is at the sixteenth. He has been at the sixteenth for nineteen years and has never advanced past it, and every note in the college's file about his own case uses the word pending.

His advantage is that he is the only reader in that office who can work inside the seal at all, because he is the only body in it that is not a visitor, and he hears the object — every sound it makes is legible to him as a position — so he navigates by the vault rather than by light and can be in the dark where the descent's reading is taken. His cost is the same body in both halves. One resonator means one flank or the other and never both, so the frame he is certifying others against cannot itself be certified. And a vaultborn's frame takes its shape from whatever it is standing on, which means his own certification would require him to stand on two surfaces and that every plate he has ever stood on is the plate he was read on, so he is the one body in the record that cannot be moved between plates and therefore cannot be certified under the rule that requires it.

So the college's second reader is the only reader it cannot certify. That is a vacancy rather than a person, and the office has responded the only way a vacancy can be responded to: by calling him pending, which is a status, not a refusal, and which costs the college nothing and can be renewed indefinitely. His eleven refusals were the last act of the arrangement in which anybody believed he would eventually be seated.

Nothing here is a plot against him. The seal is running, the reading is being taken, the cycle turns, and the college has a rule about certifying a frame and a body that the rule cannot reach. He has kept the reading for four centuries by refusing his own eleven times rather than the once that would have settled it, and he has never said why the eleventh mattered.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on a descent plate with one hand flat on the seal's inner surface and his head turned toward a sound the vault had not made yet, and telling the reader behind him that the plate was the wrong one before anything had been read.
canon.lore:
There is a population in this setting that was not descended and not born. It was sealed inside an object and it has answered that object's resonance ever since, and everything else about it follows from that single fact. Its qi comes from one resonator. It hears the object — every sound the object makes is legible to it as a position — and it navigates by that rather than by light. It is arranged along the object's inner surfaces and it takes its shape from whatever it is standing on, and the record is careful to say that this anatomy is unsettled and under-described and that nobody who has been inside the seal has come back with consistent measurements. There is no wilderness population and there never has been one. Remove the object and they stop, and no technique, item or realm changes that.

Its ceiling is the seventeenth gate and the reason is arithmetic rather than difficulty. The flank vessels need two pressures held at the same time. A vaultborn has exactly one pressure source, and one resonator can pressurise one flank or the other and never both, so the species clears the reservoirs and the heels without difficulty and loses at the flanks. The vessels are not hard. The supply is one. This is the same shape as the marshfolk wall and it is not the same wall at all: a marshfolk has no structure for a heel and this body has one structure too few for a pair.

Ithamar is at the sixteenth and has been for nineteen years, and the mortuary college that employs him describes his own case as pending rather than refused, because a vacancy and a refusal are different states in this setting's vocabulary and only one of them can be renewed without a decision. He is the second reader for the Storm Crypt. The office certifies that a frame which came up through a re-form of the seal is the same frame that went down, because the seal re-cuts its population on a cycle while a description belongs to the surface that produced it.

He has signed every entry in that vault for four centuries. He has refused his own eleven times. Nobody in the office knows why the eleventh was refused when the first ten were accepted, and he has not been asked, because the question would have to be answered by a body that cannot be certified and the college has a form for certification and not for the other kind of answer.

His frame is the difficulty in its plainest form. A vaultborn takes its shape from whatever surface it stands on. The college's own practice is to move a frame between plates before it will read it twice, because a gain that appears on two plates is a gain and a gain that appears on one plate is the plate. Every plate he has ever stood on is a plate he has been read on, and a frame that cannot be moved off its own reading cannot be read twice, so the rule that would certify him cannot be satisfied by him. He is the one body in the record whose own certification would require a surface he has never stood on and would not recognise if he did.

The work itself he is the best instrument in the setting for. He is the only reader who can be inside the seal during a descent, because he is not a visitor to it, and he navigates by the vault's own sound in the dark where the reading is taken. He has kept four centuries of descent continuity because the person holding the second plate is the person who is already inside the room. That is a real and unmatched qualification. It is also the reason nobody can replace him, which is the same fact as the qualification, and the reason he can never be seated, which is not the same fact as either.

He asked, in the correct form, to be seated rather than continued, and was given the answer the vocabulary has for a thing that cannot be decided yet. He has not asked again. He has kept the reading, refused his own eleven times, and declined to explain the eleventh, and the only person in this setting who could have asked him about it has been dead for a very long time and left a body in a vault that re-cuts its own population, so the question cannot be asked of the only witness who would have understood the answer.
history: Was formed against the last plate he stood on inside the seal, which is the ordinary way a vaultborn comes into being and the reason nobody inside can describe their own measurements.
Was found by the Field Registry's first reader on a descent and was assessed twice on two plates, and was the first body in the vault whose certification was returned unresolved rather than refused.
Took the second reader's post at the age the record gives as unconvertible, on the reasoning that the reading needs somebody who is already inside the room.
Cleared the sixteenth gate and has held it for nineteen years, which is as far as one resonator can carry a body and one gate further than that.
Refused his own certification eleven times, and the eleventh refusal is the one nobody has asked him about, and he has not been asked.

He has not been in a fight in four centuries and has been described completely and correctly by people who have never had to test any of it.
